ai.title: Refactor SDK runtime URL resolution into getRuntimeAppUrlFromEnv
ai.summary: Extracts `NEXT_PUBLIC_CODEBUFF_APP_URL` and `CODEBUFF_APP_URL` lookup logic from `getWebsiteUrl` into a new exported helper `getRuntimeAppUrlFromEnv` in `sdk/src/env.ts`. This centralizes runtime override handling for remote hosts bundling the SDK, preventing bundle-time localhost URL inlining issues. The change affects `sdk/src/constants.ts` and `sdk/src/env.ts`, updating the internal resolution mechanism while preserving existing behavior.

eli5.text: When the Codebuff tool needs to find its own address while running on a remote server or in another app's backend, it now looks that address up the same standardized way every time instead of grabbing a possibly-stale address baked in at build time. This stops remote hosts (like cloud functions that include Codebuff's code) from accidentally trying to reach a developer's local machine address that they can never access. If the Codebuff team or anyone embedding Codebuff looks at the logs, the URL resolution should be more predictable and no longer silently point at a localhost address that doesn't exist in the deployed environment. It's live today, affecting only the behind-the-scenes setup for apps that bundle Codebuff's toolkit.

ai.summary: The SDK run loop now forwards the run AbortSignal into each tool call. handleToolCall in sdk/src/run.ts threads signal through to run_terminal_command, read_url, code_search, and callMCPTool, and each tool registers an abort listener that terminates its child process. code-search.ts and read-url.ts also propagate cancellation outward to the run, so a user interrupt mid-step resolves cleanly instead of leaving a hung child.

ai.title: CLI ships terminal watchdog for uncatchable exits
ai.summary: A new in-process watchdog in `cli/src/utils/terminal-watchdog.ts` spawns a detached `/bin/sh` process that writes `TERMINAL_RESET_SEQUENCES` to the inherited tty stdout only after this process disappears, covering SIGKILL, native crashes, and process-group kill sweeps that bypass both the renderer-cleanup handlers and the npm wrapper (which is also absent for direct-binary or dev runs). The clean-shutdown path calls `stopTerminalWatchdog()` synchronously before terminal reset and renderer destroy, and the new sequences `\x1b[<u` and `\x1b[>4;0m` were also added to `SAFE_TERMINAL_RESET_SEQUENCES` in all three npm wrapper scripts, with a test asserting each wrapper literal stays in sync with the shared constant. Three other mechanical changes are bundled: a smoke-test shim, the shared sequence constant extraction, and early-fatal-handler reordering; none alter user-facing commands.
ai.evidence: Commit 3d1a8e68 adds cli/src/utils/terminal-reset-sequences.ts (exports `TERMINAL_RESET_SEQUENCES`) and cli/src/utils/terminal-watchdog.ts (exports `startTerminalWatchdog`, `stopTerminalWatchdog`); cli/src/index.tsx calls `startTerminalWatchdog()` before renderer creation and `stopTerminalWatchdog()` in the early fatal handler and cleanup path; renderer-cleanup.ts imports `TERMINAL_RESET_SEQUENCES` from the new module; the three npm wrapper scripts cli/release/index.js, cli/release-staging/index.js, and freebuff/cli/release/index.js each gain the two new sequences `\x1b[<u` and `\x1b[>4;0m`.
